newsitem.title: BELGIUM: New food labelling rules are unworkable say Greens.
newsitem.headline: New food labelling rules are unworkable say Greens.

text.p: New European Union laws on labelling novel foodstuffs, due to come into force on May 15, are deeply flawed and practically unworkable, Green Euro-MPs said on Tuesday.

The provisions of Regulation 258/97 were so unclear as to leave room for widely differing interpretations and yet the European Commission, which drafted the proposal, was unable to tell Euro-MPs how it should be read, Belgian Green Paul Lannye told a news conference.
"They are the authors of this regulation and they can't explain it...even though the regulation comes into effect in two days' time," he said.

Two weeks ago the Green group asked the Commission to answer a series of concerns about the new labelling rules, which the Greens have consistently attacked as limited in scope, impractical and too lax on the labelling of genetically modified organisms (GMOs).
"It is completely impossible to implement these provisions," German Green Hiltrud Breyer told reporters.
Among their concerns the Greens wanted to know if gene maize, gene soya and other GMO products which have already been cleared for sale, would now be considered novel foods and have to be labelled.
The Euro-MPs also wanted assurances that novel ingredients would be banned from baby food, as recommended by the EU's Scientific Committee on Food.
But on Monday the Commission said it needed at least another week to come up with the answers.

Last month the EU's Standing Committee on Foodstuffs, composed of experts from the 15 member states, backed a proposal to extend the labelling rules for novel foods to cover GMOs but delayed a final decision until June.
Gene-modified soybeans developed by Monsanto and a maize strain developed by Ciba Geigy, which were approved for sale by the EU last year, would both be affected.
